originalTurnBoundary.rule: original = main-session rows with timestamp < first follow-up queue-operation; the follow-up queue-operation/user/attachment/assistant rows are excluded

resumedOriginalCalls.evidence: No SendMessage tool_use in main or subagent transcripts; each of the 3 Agent tool_use calls has a distinct toolUseId/agentId, no agentId reuse, each subagent transcript starts with a fresh root user row (parentUuid null). All 3 Agent calls had run_in_background=false.

currentShell.scope: Bash tool shell of the follow-up turn, checked at audit time (06:26+)

originalProcess.scope: Environment of the original Claude Code process is not recorded in the JSONL and was not inspected; current-shell status is not evidence for it

limitations: assistantTurns counts distinct requestId per instance; the JSONL splits one API response into one row per content block (assistantTranscriptRows).

requestedModel and perTurnEffort are read from per-row fields in the transcript; they record the requested/effective values as logged, not how they were chosen (e.g. env var vs default vs agent definition).

No Agent call set a model or effort override (inputs contain only description, subagent_type, run_in_background, and a stray subtype_type on the first call), so any values come from defaults/agent definition.
Sub-agent transcripts have no end marker; finalTimestamp is the last timestamped row. Subagent files were last modified 06:15 and contain no follow-up rows.
Main-session original counts exclude non-timestamped rows (last-prompt, ai-title, atis-latch) which cannot be time-bounded.

The main reply earlier reported the planner as a single call; transcripts show a 3-deep nested chain of gem-upgrade-planner agents (a73bf3e905c7a425b -> aa5b9aa897a48e1ea -> a5ee63f856944f4c9). The earlier report's 'no subagent tool' note comes from the depth-3 agent.

Main transcript file is still being appended by the follow-up, so its SHA256 covers the file as of audit time, including follow-up rows; it will differ from a later download. Subagent file hashes are stable.
Findings were not independently re-validated against the experiment logs; this audit covers only session metadata.
